Subject: Security exhibit redlines + preferred pen-test window

Monica,

Thanks for sending the draft security exhibit. We're close, but legal had two asks before we can proceed to procurement: one on the pen-test timing (we prefer a quarterly window aligned to our change freeze) and one asking that SOC 2 evidence retention be clarified (they want 12 months of access to specific attestation artifacts).

I've attached our internal checklist for evidence handoff so you can see what they expect. Can you loop in your legal team and propose final language we can sign off on?

High level asks: 
- Pen-test window: avoid our monthly release week (first week of each month); prefer the 3rd week of quarter.
- Evidence retention: specify which SOC 2 artifacts are shared and for how long.

If easier, happy to jump on a 30-min call with legal tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Tom Jennings
Lead InfoSec, Greenfield Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tom Jennings <tom.jennings@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines + preferred pen-test window

Tom / Monica / team — I reviewed the attached redline and drafted targeted language to address both asks. Key points in the draft: 

1) Pen-test timing: we can commit to quarterly pen-test windows scheduled in advance and exclude Greenfield's first-of-month release week. Preferred primary windows: the 3rd week of each fiscal quarter; we also propose a single fallback week for urgent security engagements (with 14-day notice).

2) SOC 2 evidence: propose granular list of artifacts we will make available (SOC 2 report, control mappings, summary of relevant logs, and attestation letter). Retention/access window: 12 months from the date of request for the artifacts listed. We purposely avoid broad "unlimited audit access" language — instead we provide a time-bound evidence access process and agree to facilitate reasonable vendor assessments.

3) Operational notes: Marcus — can you confirm if 14-day notice is sufficient for the fallback pen-test window and whether we can lock the 3rd-week windows as recurring calendar holds?

4) Minor redlines: removed any commitment to on-prem inspection without prior security approvals; maintained obligation to redact customer PII from shared artifacts.

I've attached the text snippets (use with the exhibit) and inline comments in the DOCX. If Greenfield agrees, legal is OK with these as the final exhibit and we can update the order form term and push to procurement.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
attachments: exhibit_snippets_for_redline.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Tom Jennings <tom.jennings@greenfieldhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines + preferred pen-test window

Karthik / Monica — appreciate the quick turn. The proposed language looks reasonable; two small asks before we sign: 

1) Can the fallback "urgent" window notice be 21 days instead of 14? Our change team needs the extra buffer for scheduling.
2) For SOC 2 artifacts, please include a short list example in the exhibit (SOC 2 report, bridge letter, control narrative, and the consolidated exception log) so procurement doesn't re-open the list later.

If you can accept those two edits, we'll route to procurement and expect to return an executed order form within 5 business days. Call is not necessary unless you prefer one — we can handle by email.

Tom Jennings
Lead InfoSec, Greenfield Health
